CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys for possible congenital anomalies associated with Smith-Magenis syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3-week gestational age twin female with Smith-Magenis syndrome, diagnosed by neurology due to delayed motor milestones (not walking or sitting independently by age 1 year). She was born weighing 4 pounds 8 ounces. Perinatal history notable for feeding difficulties with apneic episodes during feeding and temperature regulation problems. She currently has severe gastroesophageal reflux and is intolerant to cow's milk. She is enrolled in multiple therapies including feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and will begin speech therapy in the next couple of weeks. She has also been evaluated by gastroenterology, allergy, neurology, orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. Currently crawling and attempting to take steps. Voids 8-10 wet diapers per 24-hour period. Fluid intake includes pea protein milk (Ripple), water, and occasionally water with small amount of juice. Twin sister is age-appropriate without known problems. Mother concerned about possible kidney involvement given family history discussion with geneticist regarding syndromic kidney anomalies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for gastroesophageal reflux, cow's milk intolerance, and delayed motor development. Denies other concerning systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis syndrome. Gastroesophageal reflux. Developmental delay. History of feeding difficulties and apneic episodes with feeding as newborn. Temperature regulation difficulties as newborn.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk intolerance.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother (age 9) with autism. Twin sister without known medical problems. No family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or transplantation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives in Dallas, Georgia with family including 9-year-old brother and twin sister.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs auscultated. Ears examined.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 3/7-week gestational age twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in association with this chromosomal deletion syndrome. Will obtain screening ultrasound of kidneys today. If abnormalities identified on ultrasound, will determine next steps and future follow-up. If normal ultrasound, no need for further nephrology follow-up. Follow-up location will be at Kennesaw/Town Center location given family residence in Dallas, Georgia.
